UI verification · re-check after fix

T017 Questions Screen Re-check

Device iPhone 17 simulator Text size AX3XL Date 12 Sep 2026
Since then. What a screen reader says, which this run could not capture, has since been recorded twice: TalkBack’s exact wording for nine events on an Android emulator (Android lane) and VoiceOver’s caption panel for eleven events on a real iPad (iPad lane).
FAIL

One of the two fixes landed; the other throws. The error message is now folded into the question label’s accessible name, exactly as required. But the scroll-to-error never runs — measureLayout rejects its target, the callback never fires, and the scroll offset stays where it was. At the largest text size the error still renders entirely above the viewport, so the tap still looks like it did nothing.

The scroll offset never moved

The scroll view spans y = 116 → 874 (758 pt of viewport). These are the accessibility-tree frames of the same four elements, read immediately before and immediately after the Continue tap.

Required question label — after

Continue button — before → after
713.99 → 893.67
Δ 0.00 pt
The label’s y is byte-identical across the tap. The two screenshots do differ, but only because the 171.67 pt error block was inserted into the layout and pushed everything below it down ~180 pt — which is why Continue moved while the scroll did not. The error’s own box ends at y = 32, above the viewport top of 116, so nothing of it is on screen.

What the user sees at AX3XL

Why it fails

The log recorded the throw the moment Continue was tapped. The callback that would have called scrollTo is never reached.

setup.log · line 14
ERROR  Warning: ref.measureLayout must be called with a ref to a native component.

Code: ScreenScaffold.tsx
  25 |   const content: Focusable | number | null = scroll.getInnerViewNode();
  26 |   if (content == null) return;
> 27 |   node.measureLayout(content, (_left, top) =>
  28 |     scroll.scrollTo({ x: 0, y: Math.max(0, top - spacing.md), animated: true }),
  29 |   );

Call Stack
  scrollFieldIntoView (src/components/ScreenScaffold.tsx:27:21)
  scrollToField      (src/components/ScreenScaffold.tsx:47:55)
  onContinue         (src/app/econsult/questions.tsx:84:20)
a11y-after.txt · the toast is a real on-screen element
label: "!, Warning: ref.measureLayout must be called with a ref to a native component."
rect:  { x: 10, y: 787.67, w: 382, h: 48 }

The toast itself is a dev-mode overlay. In a release build the warning is silent — the scroll failure is identical.

The accessible name, however, is correct

The second fix works, at both text sizes. The question label element gains the error on invalid submit; the three radios are untouched, which the contract allows.

a11y-after.txt · ref e36 / e37
before  label: "How long have you had this problem? (required)"
after   label: "How long have you had this problem? (required). Error: This question is required"

unchanged siblings
  label: "Less than a week"     value: "radio button, unchecked"
  label: "1 to 4 weeks"         value: "radio button, unchecked"
  label: "Longer than a month"  value: "radio button, unchecked"

At the default text size

No layout regression — but the same call throws here too, so the broken scroll is not specific to large text. It is invisible at this size only because the error happens to land inside the viewport (y = 481, within 116–874) without any scrolling at all.

Still open

  • Blocking

    The scroll-to-error does not run

    scrollFieldIntoView calls measureLayout with the value returned by getInnerViewNode(), which is rejected as a target, so scrollTo is never called. The scroll offset is unchanged across the tap at every text size.

  • Minor

    Step heading has no upper bound on Dynamic Type scaling

    Unchanged from the previous pass. “A few questions from your practice” measures 814.33 pt tall at AX3XL against a 758 pt viewport.

  • Not verified

    Announcement and screen-reader focus

    VoiceOver was not running, and neither focus nor announcements could be captured here. Neither was confirmed nor refuted here; it needs a VoiceOver pass.
